title: Decomposition Lens: request-unravel UX for tracing & correlation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Our Console currently provides span timelines and basic trace navigation, but customers building LLM applications ask for faster root-cause discovery across correlated requests (correlation IDs), clearer span grouping for high fan-out models, and a low-friction workflow to go from KPI anomaly to exact request payload and inference timeline. Goal: Design an investigative 'Decomposition Lens' UX that surfaces correlated sessions, a compact but expressive span timeline, correlation-first filters, and a lightweight inline payload inspector. This ticket captures the prototype explorations, trade-offs, and handoff artifacts for design + engineering implementation. Scope: - Entry points: anomaly to trace, trace list to decomposition lens, linkouts from model-rollout diffs. - Main surface: header with correlation ID and quick actions (copy, open raw request, open in workspace). - Timeline: compressed row-per-service with span grouping heuristics, multi-scale zoom, and highlight for KV cache hits/misses. - Filters: correlation-scoped presets (by model version, region, route), adjustable time window, and span-type toggles. - Payload inspector: collapsible panel showing request metadata, prompt tokens (redacted by policy), and deterministic replay link. - Performance constraints: must render traces up to 10k spans in <= 600ms on median enterprise dataset (engineering to validate). Out of scope: full session-replay video, advanced anomaly detection UI.
design_proposals: Proposal A - Compact Stack: single-column timeline with collapsible service lanes and inline span summaries; prioritizes density for long traces.
Proposal B - Sidecar Decomposer: timeline on left, detailed span list + payload inspector sidecar on right for focused debugging flows.
Proposal C - Correlation-Focused Mode: filter-first modal that surfaces sibling requests sharing correlation IDs before entering full timeline.
Chosen approach: Hybrid (Proposal B with quick correlation modal) — balances density and context while keeping payload inspector discoverable without losing timeline space.
acceptance_criteria: Design mockups (desktop) for three breakpoints: 1200px, 1440px, 1920px with sidecar flow
Interactive Figma prototype demonstrating: correlation modal -> open trace -> expand span -> inspect payload
List of accessibility considerations (keyboard nav, focus states, readable color contrast for span types)
Annotated handoff for ENG describing span grouping heuristics and expected telemetry keys
Usability test notes (5 engineers/product folks) showing task completion for 'find root span for correlation' in under 90s on prototype

decisions: Use Sidecar Decomposer as base layout (timeline + right-side payload/metadata inspector)
Expose correlation-first modal as primary entry for anomaly workflows
Group spans by callsite by default with user override to group by service
Show span-level KV cache hit/miss icon with hover tooltip instead of full textual field
Mask prompt tokens by default; show deterministic checksum and truncated preview with explicit 'Reveal' action requiring permission
